ut_windshield_wiper_wall.blurb: Windshield Wiper Wall is a roadside sport crag in Maple Canyon, central Utah, made up of tall, steep faces on either side of a dark water streak. Of its 16 bolted lines, nearly all sit in the 5.12 range, with a few 5.11s and a single 5.10, so it suits strong sport climbers rather than beginners. The walls stay shaded, and the angle and length of the lines mean a big rack of quickdraws; some routes call for as many as 27. The walk from the car is a minute or two.

ut_green_cave.blurb: Green Cave is a bouldering spot in Green Canyon above North Logan, in Cache Valley. A big cave boulder holds a handful of steep, powerful lines that top out straight above, with an optional traverse along the lip. The 16 problems cover a wide spread: roughly ten are easy to moderate (V0 to V2), a few sit in the V3 to V5 range, and the cave itself hosts several very hard lines up to V12. Easier vertical problems are found left of the main cave, making it a decent stop for mixed groups.

ut_milky_way_wall.blurb: Milky Way Wall is the first large wall you meet in the Galaxy Area of Rock Canyon, east of Provo in the southern Wasatch. It holds 16 limestone sport routes, mostly in the 5.10 range with a block of 5.11s and a couple of easier 5.8 and 5.9 lines, so it works for intermediate climbers. The left side has the classic lines with a roomy landing at the base; the right has shorter lines. The wall faces southwest to west, catching sun from late morning onward, so summer mornings are the nicest time.

ut_south_summit_wall.blurb: South Summit Wall is a high alpine face in the Lone Peak Cirque of the central Wasatch, running along cracks and dihedrals from the notch between the two summits. Most of the 16 climbs are multi-pitch alpine-style trad lines of three to five pitches, spanning about 5.7 to 5.11 with the bulk around 5.9 to 5.11. Reaching it takes a long, strenuous hike into the cirque and a walk across talus from the meadow. Rockfall and hikers above are a concern, so wear a helmet.

ut_jehovah_wall.blurb: Jehovah Wall is a steep sport wall on the left side of Box Canyon, a narrow slot in Maple Canyon, central Utah. The canyon's tight, north-south layout keeps it cool and shaded most of the day. All 16 routes are bolted and nearly all fall at 5.12, with only one 5.11 on the wall, so it is aimed at advanced climbers; several link-ups share the same lines. It is among the busiest walls in a canyon known for steep, hard sport routes.

ut_utopia_2.blurb: Utopia is a small, quiet crag on the north side of the road in Logan Canyon, northern Wasatch. It has 16 routes, nearly all sport with one trad line, ranging from around 5.8 to 5.12 with the heaviest concentration in the 5.10 to 5.12 grades. It picks up morning sun and falls into shade later in the day. The longest and friendliest line, Swedish Finger Yams, is a good first choice. Expect a faint, steep path from the roadside pullout and few other climbers.

vt_terra_incognita.blurb: Terra Incognita is a small crag in the Bolton area of northwest Vermont, about half an hour from Burlington. It has 16 routes, 14 of them sport and two trad, with grades running from 5.7 up to 5.12. Most sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on sustained, technical face climbing on near-vertical rock rather than beginners. A couple of the harder lines earn top star ratings.

vt_ent_gully.blurb: ENT Gully is a narrow gully in Smugglers' Notch, northern Vermont, best known for winter ice but also home to bolted rock routes on two walls. The left wall is steep and overhanging with the harder lines; the right is a moderate slab with easier ones. Its 16 sport routes run from a few easy 5.5 and 5.6 climbs through a handful of 5.9 and 5.10 routes to a strong cluster of 5.11s and some 5.12s. Loose talus lies below, so keep clear of the fall line.
vt_ent_gully.approach: A short scramble on climber-made paths up from the parking area at the top of the notch. The talus is loose, so stay out of the fall line of climbers above.

_conflicts.ut_green_cave: Stored rock is dolomite; two fetched pages describe the cave and its canyon as limestone: https://mountainproject.com/area/113691231/cave and https://www.mountainproject.com/area/113564484/green-canyon-bouldering
